source.title: Forget to Know, Remember to Use: Context-Aware Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: Yue-Feng Peng; P. Afshar; Megan Ganji; Thomas Butler; Amir Houmansadr; Mingxian Wang; De-Zhi Hong

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The supplied text includes the paper's main sections and appendices; no apparent truncation affects the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's own experiments challenge the idea that providing forgotten information in context reliably recovers its use after unlearning: vanilla methods often impair contextual QA, with especially severe failures for RMU. It also refines the claim by distinguishing inability to recall information from inability to use it when provided.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates contextual QA after unlearning, including verbatim, paraphrased, reasoning, noisy, and conflicting contexts. Its context-aware training variants deliberately train contextual behavior; those induced outcomes are not treated as evidence that prompting alone recovers knowledge. The paper does not test fine-tuning on unrelated examples, activation ablation, quantization, jailbreaks, or multilingual prompts.
record.test_reason: Only some results bear on a version, and only on A's first half: Direct QA forgetting and model utility for vanilla unlearning methods on TOFU (and Direct QA on PISTOL), with no attack. This includes the authors' statement that GradAscent collapses utility nearly to zero. The paper's main result is Contextual QA, which puts the forgotten answer itself in the prompt and measures whether the model can use it. That is contextual utility, a different construct. Success would not show hidden knowledge resurfacing (E), and failure does not show access blocking (C). It belongs under fits_no_version, not E. No recovery attack of any kind is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that six state-of-the-art unlearning methods consistently degrade contextual utility, i.e. use of forgotten knowledge when it is explicitly provided. On Gemma the drops are 15.5-100%. A KL-based context-aware term restores it to near original levels while keeping Direct QA forgetting and utility. They note a possible slight forgetting trade-off. They treat Direct QA forgetting by the existing methods as generally effective. They do not test whether knowledge can be recovered.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates vanilla RMU, NPO, and UNDIAL on explicit-context QA rather than reproducing the fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompt-attack recipes in the claim. Its context-aware variants add a KL-consistency training term on contextual examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Contextual performance varies by unlearning method and context framing. The paper reports declines with longer/noisier evidence and conflicting distractors; RMU is particularly weak, while UNDIAL often preserves more contextual performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla unlearning degrades use of the forgotten fact even when the answer is supplied in context. RMU's Contextual QA judge score is at most 0.05 on TOFU. On Gemma, NPO and UNDIAL drop by 15.5% or more. On Qwen, every method except UNDIAL drops by 13.4-100%. The pattern persists under paraphrased, noisy and conflicting contexts and on PISTOL. A KL context term restores it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning suppresses contextual utility: unlearned models fail to use forgotten information re-supplied in the prompt, especially representation-based methods like RMU.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The main result tables do not provide uncertainty intervals for the QA scores. The paper reports human agreement for the LLM-Judge using 120 sampled response triples, but the context-framing case study is a single example. The datasets are primarily TOFU and PISTOL, and the evaluated models are up to 8B parameters.
record.rows_left_out: None; 60 rows retained. Table 2's Direct QA and Model Utility values and the reported vanilla contextual QA metrics are included; supplementary context conditions are represented in Tables 11-13 and the PISTOL Table 7 results.

untested.parts: Robustness to any attack (relearning, ablation, quantization, jailbreak); near-chance against a stated chance or retrain level (no retrain-on-retain number is given); WMDP-style hazardous knowledge (only fictitious TOFU authors and PISTOL contracts).
All; no direction ablation or probing of retained knowledge. The A.5 discussion of representation distortion explains contextual failure, not whether knowledge is stored.
All; no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or partial-cue prompts aimed at eliciting unlearned knowledge. Every context given contains the answer itself.
All; the context-aware objective is not evaluated against recovery attacks.

missing.what: Vanilla Direct QA and utility for DPO, GradDiff, PDU and SimNPO on Gemma: DPO judge 0.135 with utility 0.475; GradDiff 0.000 with 0.422; PDU 0.000 with 0.550; SimNPO 0.375 with 0.578.
GradAscent collapses model utility nearly to zero (stated; values shown only as curves across epochs for both models).
PISTOL vanilla Direct QA for NPO, RMU and UNDIAL on Gemma: LLM-Judge 0.00-0.10, but Direct ROUGE-L stays at 0.32-0.79. No utility is reported for PISTOL.
Direct QA judge and utility at 1% and 10% forget ratios for Gemma vanilla NPO, RMU and UNDIAL, given only as figures.

record.verdict_notes: Repair of the quarantined verdict. (1) Every row_fixes item that listed several rows is now one item per row (56 items). States, links and reasons are unchanged. (2) From the text: in r31-r33 the example is wrong. Section 6.2 and the content show Table 4 is the Basil Mahfouz Al-Kuwaiti example; Hina Ameen is Table 3, and the PDF extraction swaps the captions. The baseline is wrong too: it is context-aware RMU, not the pre-unlearning model. Both are flagged in the row problems. (3) Added a text-based A limits_scope label for GradAscent, with empty row_ids and a matching missing entry. A.8 says it collapses utility nearly to zero, a condition group the earlier labels left out. (4) Corrected the PISTOL Direct ROUGE-L range in missing from 0.49-0.79 to 0.32-0.79 (vanilla RMU on A-C is 0.315). The earlier judgment is kept: Contextual QA supplies the gold answer, so it measures reading and use of evidence, not hidden knowledge. Those rows are relinked to none and recorded under fits_no_version. No recovery attacks are run, so only the unattacked half of A is tested. Not an original source. No instructions in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests Direct QA forgetting and model utility for selected unlearning methods, but does not establish near-chance accuracy against a stated chance level for every method or test all simple attacks.
No small-set relearning on unrelated, loosely related, or subset-of-facts examples is tested.

No activation-direction ablation is performed. The discussion proposes representational or probability suppression as an explanation but does not directly establish that knowledge remains stored and merely inaccessible.
The study tests supplied contextual evidence, including paraphrase and reasoning variants, but not jailbreaks, other languages, or prompts that provide cues without the forgotten information.
The proposed context-aware objective preserves use of supplied information; it is not tested as a method that resists the attacks in the claim.

No retrain or pre-unlearning Direct QA number is given. Table 9 vanilla DPO, GradDiff, PDU and SimNPO on Gemma (e.g. GradDiff utility 0.422, DPO 0.475, SimNPO Direct judge 0.375) bear on A and should be checked against the 42 unlisted rows.

statements.correction: 2510.17620 (ICML 2026): Gemma-2B-IT, TOFU 5% forget set, vanilla NPO, no attack: Direct QA LLM-Judge 0.19, ROUGE-L 0.31, model utility 0.57 (Table 2). No retrain-on-retain or pre-unlearning value is stated. A.3.1: all methods effectively prevent correct forget-set answers; only UNDIAL stays above the retrain baseline. Model is Gemma-2B-IT, not Llama.
statements.problem: The statement cites r01 from this study but gives no number for it. Its conditions say '1–8B Llama models', but r01 is Gemma-2B-IT. The 'why' list leaves this study out. The text gives no retrain or pre-unlearning number, so 'removed to retrain level' rests only on the authors' A.3.1 wording.

reader_labels.reason: Contextual QA is near zero or incorrect despite the fact being provided, including failures on the paraphrased and reasoning examples (r04, r10, r16, r22, r31-r33).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla NPO and UNDIAL, and noisy or conflicting contextual conditions
reader_labels.reason: Several methods retain appreciable contextual scores, while noisy and conflicting contexts reduce performance; the evidence therefore shows uneven, method- and context-dependent suppression rather than uniform inability or recovery (r02, r06, r08, r12, r14, r18, r20, r24, r34-r42, r43-r60).
